'''Heisook Lee''' ({{langx|ko|이혜숙}}, born 1948{{r|born}}) is a South Korean mathematician and activist for gender equality in mathematics. She is retired as a professor of mathematics and dean at [[Ewha Womans University]]. Her mathematical research has concerned [[abstract algebra]] and [[algebraic coding theory]], including work on [[Dual code|self-dual code]]s and [[bent function]]s.

Lee graduated from Ewha Womans University in 1971. After a master's degree in 1974 from the [[University of British Columbia]] in Canada, she completed a Ph.D. in 1978 from [[Queen's University at Kingston]], also in Canada.{{r|gsum}} Her dissertation, '' The Brauer Group of an Integral Scheme'', was supervised by Morris Orzech.{{r|mg}}

After postdoctoral research in Germany at the [[University of Regensburg]], she returned to Ewha Womans University in 1980, as a professor of mathematics.{{r|x}} She became dean of natural sciences and dean of research affairs from 1997 to 2001, and dean of graduate studies from 2006 to 2008.{{r|gsum}}

Lee became founding editor of ''Communications of the Korean Mathematical Society'' in 1986. From 1994 to 1996, she was editor in chief of the ''Journal of the Korean Mathematical Society''.{{r|gsum}} She was the second president of the Korea Federation of Women's Science & Technology Associations (KOFWST), serving from 2006 to 2007.{{r|kofwst}} She founded the Center for Women in Science, Engineering, and Technology (WISET), now the Korean Foundation for Women in Science, Engineering, and Technology, and became its first president, serving from 2013 to 2016.{{r|wiset}}

She is a professor emeritus at Ewha Womans University,{{r|gsum}} and president of the Korea Center for Gendered Innovations (GISTeR).{{r|gister}}
